profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer | Linux System, Kernel | Networking, Telecom | Cloud (Azure, Nexus, AWS) | C/C++, Golang | Bash, Python | Virtualization, Containers | DevOps, Automation
profile.jobTitle: Senior Software Engineer, Azure for Operators
profile.summary:
Summary:
Passionate Senior Software Engineer specializing in Linux systems, telecom, and networking. Proven track record of improving system performance and security. Expert in automation, virtualization, and cloud technologies with extensive success leading engineering projects.

Details:
I am a Senior Software Engineer with considerable Linux experience.  In fact, I am passionate about Linux!  I've maintained my main computer either personally, professionally, or both with the main OS as Linux for most of this time.  By supporting myself, I have learned so much about how Linux works even down to the Linux kernel.  I am the Linux expert at my job and enjoy sharing my deep Linux knowledge with my coworkers.  As I understand not only programing, but also the OS, I have also been able to help our IT departments at times.
 
Several years ago, I was the base "team" for the vMME telecom product.  When we set out to virtualize the product (from a cluster of hardware nodes to a cluster of VMs), I solely created the BASE OS for it.  I crafted an optimized Ubuntu OS, created numerous startup scripts to customize the environment for vMME, optimized performance along the way, gained a deep understanding of Linux networking/routing/BFD/etc, and finally maintained and added new Linux kernel patches, mainly for TIPC and SCTP.  I still maintain this BASE OS layer which expended to also support the vSSF telecom product.

Most recently, I've adapted the vMME to work in Azure and Nexus, integrating utilities and scripts into the OS layer.

Over the years, I've also learned a lot about Telecom protocols (from 2G to 5G), networking in general, programming in various languages (such as C/C++, Golang, and Java) as well as scripting (such as bash, python, perl, expect, etc), and gained experience in various other technologies (such as DPDK, Linux Containers, Docker, Kubernetes, etc).

Open-Source contributions:
- I maintain patches to systemd and systemd-shim since 2019 for the popular (consistently ranked #1 on distrowatch.com) MX Linux distribution on GitHub (https://github.com/knelsonmeister).  The systemd-shim allows the OS to boot with either the old Sys-V init or systemd.
- I published the changes I made to the TACACS+ module for NSS, nss_tacplus, to GitHub (https://github.com/kevinnelson-affirmed).  This module is used in vMME, vSSF, and Unity Cloud.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer, Azure for Operators
positions.description:
Lead engineer for vMME (a cluster of Linux VMs providing 2G-4G mobility):
•	Automate the building of 3 BASE OS layers by scripting manual processes, reducing build time from hours to minutes, and automate HTML report generation for security issues (CVEs) fixed in the load.
•	Convert 8 vMME Jenkins loadbuilds to YAML pipelines in Azure DevOps (ADO) by creating a build container that mimics the on-prem build VM, allowing Microsoft’s scans (CodeQL, Component Governance, etc.) to run on the codebase, leading to better quality and security.
•	Pioneer the deployment of vMME using Azure CLI commands on the Microsoft Nexus platform, reducing the time for several other products to get started on Nexus.
•	Debug and modify our TIPC Linux kernel patches for several operators, resulting in customers no longer getting dropped and higher capacity for the system.
•	Automate the deployment of vMME on KVM directly by heavily modifying a Python script from another product, enabling customers to save money by switching from OpenStack to KVM.
•	Add SR-IOV support for vMME in Azure, Nexus, and KVM, enabling better performance and thus higher capacity support.
positions.insights: Computer Networking, Shell Scripting and +15 skills

positions.title: Consulting Software Engineer
positions.description:
Lead engineer for vMME (a cluster of Linux VMs providing 2G-4G mobility):
•	Increased capacity of vMME on Azure and AWS by implementing a Golang program utilizing Azure/AWS APIs to dynamically moving loopback IPs when VMs were locked/down.
•	Increased the number of LTE radios (eNBs) that can connect to the vMME by modifying the SCTP Linux kernel code to hash on more tuple info allowing for a faster association lookup.
•	Fixed TIPC bugs in the Linux kernel by using slub_debug and ftrace tools resulting in no more kernel panics, and thus better stability of the vMME product.
•	Added a firewall to the Data VM of the vMME by writing a Golang program that programmed iptables rules thus adding better security to the product.
positions.insights: Amazon Web Services (AWS), Computer Networking and +13 skills

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
Lead engineer for BASE OS of vMME (cluster of Linux VMs providing 2G-4G mobility):
•	Personally created a Python script that uses Confd//Tailf Python API to monitor config. When used in conjunction with incron.d, a script can be kicked off when config changes resulting in quicker development of several features that would have required C++.
•	Enabled vMME users with limited privileges to see logs from all VMs directly from the active MGMT VM by integrating sshfs into the BASE OS and adding scripts to mount the log directory from each VM resulting in quicker debugging of issues.
•	Updated TIPC Linux kernel code to handle a dynamic broadcast MTU allowing the vMME to handle configurable MTU values.
•	Updated the open-source openapi-codegen tool to better handle 3GPP spec YAML files resulting in increased productivity for many teams doing 5G coding.
•	Got trained on a DPDK framework and wrote a DPDK prototype to debug an issue our application was having with DPDK OVS on RedHat.
positions.insights: Computer Networking, Shell Scripting and +10 skills

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer, LTE Core Development
positions.description:
Lead engineer for BASE OS of vMME (cluster of Linux VMs providing 2G-4G mobility):
•	Solely created the BASE OS for the virtualization of the MME by crafting an optimized Ubuntu OS with numerous startup scripts and integrating Linux kernel patches mainly for TIPC and SCTP resulting in a VM that boots in a few seconds with many security features enabled.
•	Wrote the C++ code that handled egress packets from non-Load Balancer (LB) VMs to LB VMs as well as from LB VMs to the Next Hop Routers (NHRs) by using Netlink APIs to program Linux routing. Default multi-path routes with multiple nethops in Equal Cost Multi-Path (ECMP) configuration were added on the main route table or in additional route tables.
positions.insights: Computer Networking, Shell Scripting and +9 skills
